permdisp.reason: PERMDISP requires at least two observations in every group.

observations.meaning: PERMANOVA location association and PERMDISP dispersion test for CT reconstruction kernel in the CT native-distance geometry.
observations.finding: CT reconstruction kernel shows a nominal PERMANOVA association (pseudo-F 1.797, p=0.048) that does not survive BH correction (q=0.054); PERMDISP is not estimable because several kernel levels have fewer than two observations.

permdisp.reason: PERMDISP requires at least two observations in every group.

observations.meaning: PERMANOVA location association and PERMDISP dispersion test for CT scanner model in the CT native-distance geometry.
observations.finding: CT scanner model shows a nominal PERMANOVA association (pseudo-F 1.453, p=0.054, q=0.054, r_squared 0.200) that does not reach BH-corrected significance; PERMDISP is not estimable because many of the 16 scanner-model levels have fewer than two observations.

observations.meaning: Distance-based regression of continuous acquisition factors on CT native-distance geometry, with its own BH family.
observations.finding: CT z-spacing (pseudo-F 16.67, q=0.002, r_squared 0.142) and CT slice thickness (pseudo-F 15.85, q=0.002, r_squared 0.136) show the strongest continuous associations; CT pixel spacing (q=0.035, r_squared 0.019) and study year (q=0.004, r_squared 0.029) are also significant but with much smaller magnitudes.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: Within the confounder_exclusion dimension, the partition shows statistically significant association with multiple technical, acquisition, and site factors, and the pattern is broad rather than isolated. In the fused geometry, tissue source site has a significant PERMANOVA location association (pseudo-F 1.014, p=0.001, q=0.0025) with a small r_squared of 0.050, and PERMDISP is not significant (p=0.434), so the site association is not accompanied by detectable dispersion differences. In the CT native-distance geometry, CT phase has the largest categorical association (pseudo-F 2.466, q=0.0025, r_squared 0.154) and also a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (q=0.0285), so its location association may reflect both centroid and dispersion differences. CT manufacturer is significant in both PERMANOVA (q=0.0067, r_squared 0.059) and PERMDISP (q=0.009), but the Philips level has only 3 patients, so that dispersion result is based on very few observations. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and CT scanner model (q=0.054) are nominally associated but do not survive BH correction, and their PERMDISP tests are not estimable because several levels have fewer than two observations. Among continuous acquisition factors, CT z-spacing (pseudo-F 16.67, q=0.002, r_squared 0.142) and CT slice thickness (pseudo-F 15.85, q=0.002, r_squared 0.136) show the strongest associations, with CT pixel spacing (q=0.035, r_squared 0.019) and study year (q=0.004, r_squared 0.029) significant but much smaller in magnitude. The categorical PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression tests belong to separate BH families, so their q-values are not directly comparable across families. These results indicate that the candidate partition is not independent of measured technical and acquisition factors, and the combination of a significant site association in the fused geometry with strong CT acquisition associations in the CT geometry suggests that some of the geometric or biological signal could be confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation, the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition, and the nonsignificant PERMDISP for tissue source site does not prove absence of confounding.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry, with no partition-level evidence of internal subdivision. The confounder results are relevant to that picture because the weak geometric separation could partly reflect technical or site-related structure rather than purely biological signal: the significant tissue source site association in the fused geometry and the strong CT z-spacing and slice thickness associations in the CT geometry indicate that the fused and CT geometries are not independent of measured technical factors. The prior biological_support reports for K4_C0001-K4_C0004 describe distinct RNA phenotypes (K4_C0001 broad OXPHOS/immune down-regulation, K4_C0002 OXPHOS/anabolic up-regulation, K4_C0003 immune/inflammatory up-regulation, K4_C0004 OXPHOS down-regulation with EMT/Hedgehog up-regulation), and the WXS report for K4_C0002 shows VHL/PBRM1 depletion. The confounder results create an unresolved tension with those biological interpretations: if site and CT acquisition factors are associated with candidate membership, some of the apparent biological distinctiveness could be partially confounded, and the biological reports do not adjust for these factors. The prior known_label_echo report showed low correspondence with ClearCode34 and TCGA m1-m4, which is also consistent with the partition capturing structure that is not aligned with standard taxonomies and could be partly technical.
limitations: Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition.
Nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding; the nonsignificant PERMDISP for tissue source site does not prove no dispersion confounding.
The categorical PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression tests belong to separate BH families, so p-values and q-values are not directly comparable across families.

Several factor levels are sparse (e.g., CT manufacturer Philips n=3; many scanner-model and kernel levels with fewer than two observations), which makes PERMDISP not estimable for kernel and scanner model and can destabilize association estimates.
The analysis uses the supplied partition and does not test alternative partitions or adjust for multiple factors simultaneously.
The r_squared values are univariable distance-based association magnitudes and must not be added or interpreted as independent causal variance explained.

observations.meaning: Magnitude and statistical evidence of categorical technical/acquisition factor association with K4_C0002 membership versus the rest, before and after BH correction within the categorical family.
observations.finding: Four categorical factors are significantly associated with K4_C0002 membership after BH correction: tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.428, q=0.0018), CT manufacturer (0.353, q=0.0018), CT reconstruction kernel (0.387, q=0.0018), and CT scanner model (0.374, q=0.0075). CT phase is nominally associated (0.250, p=0.063) but does not survive correction.

observations.meaning: Effect magnitude and statistical evidence of continuous technical/acquisition factor association with K4_C0002 membership, before and after BH correction within the continuous family.
observations.finding: CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.174, q=7.43e-05) and CT z-spacing (0.180, q=7.43e-05) are strongly and significantly associated with K4_C0002 membership; study year and pixel spacing are not significant.

observations.meaning: Observed factor-level imbalance contributing to the categorical associations for K4_C0002.
observations.finding: B8 is overrepresented in K4_C0002 (12/31 versus 7/72 in the rest) and BP underrepresented (7/31 versus 38/72); Siemens is overrepresented (17/31 versus 13/72) and GE underrepresented (14/31 versus 56/72); B30f kernel is overrepresented (9/31 versus 4/72). These imbalances drive the corrected associations.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: Within the confounder_exclusion dimension, K4_C0002 shows strong and BH-corrected associations with multiple technical, acquisition, and site factors. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.428, q=0.0018), CT manufacturer (0.353, q=0.0018), CT reconstruction kernel (0.387, q=0.0018), and CT scanner model (0.374, q=0.0075) are all significantly associated with K4_C0002 membership, and CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.174, q=7.43e-05) and CT z-spacing (0.180, q=7.43e-05) show the strongest continuous associations. The imbalance patterns are substantial: B8 overrepresentation, Siemens overrepresentation, and B30f kernel overrepresentation. These results indicate that K4_C0002 membership is not independent of measured site and CT acquisition characteristics, and the magnitude of the associations (Cramer's V up to 0.43, epsilon-squared up to 0.18) is larger than for K4_C0001. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation, and the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition. The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH families, so q-values are not directly comparable across families. The strong confounder signal for K4_C0002 is an unresolved concern for interpreting its biological phenotype.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: The prior biological_support reports for K4_C0002 described strong OXPHOS/anabolic up-regulation (NES 2.788, FDR 0.001) and the WXS report showed VHL/PBRM1 depletion. The present confounder results show that K4_C0002 has the strongest corrected technical and site associations in the partition, which creates a material tension: the biological and mutation phenotypes could be partially confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics, and the biological reports do not adjust for these factors. The prior structural_diagnostics report noted weak geometric separation, and the strong confounder signal for K4_C0002 is consistent with the possibility that some of its geometric or biological distinctiveness reflects technical structure. The prior partition-level confounder_association report found corrected tissue source site and CT acquisition associations across the partition; the K4_C0002 set-level results are consistent with and contribute to that partition-level pattern.
limitations: Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the tests do not establish that these factors drive K4_C0002 membership.
Nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding; CT phase is nominally associated but not corrected.
The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH correction families, so p-values and q-values are not directly comparable across families.
Contingency tables show sparse cells for some factor levels (e.g., CJ n=11 overall, Philips n=3 overall), which can destabilize association estimates.
The analysis uses the supplied partition and does not test alternative partitions or adjust for multiple factors simultaneously.

observations.meaning: Number of patients represented in each candidate set of the four-set partition.
observations.finding: The partition comprises four sets of unequal size, ranging from 13 to 39 patients, with the smallest set roughly one-third the size of the largest.

observations.meaning: Average fused affinity among patients assigned to the same candidate set, reflecting within-set cohesion in the four-view patient geometry.
observations.finding: Within-set affinity is similar across all four sets (approximately 0.0094 to 0.0101), with the smallest set K4_C0004 showing the highest within-set affinity and the largest set K4_C0001 the lowest.

observations.meaning: Magnitude of the dominant spectral eigengap within each candidate set's internal affinity structure.
observations.finding: Each set shows a large leading eigengap, but the corresponding screen_candidate_k is 1 for every set, so these leading gaps describe dominance of the single-cluster resolution rather than evidence of internal multi-cluster subdivision.

observations.meaning: Full eigengap profile across candidate resolutions within each set, showing the location and magnitude of spectral gaps.
observations.finding: In every set the first eigengap is orders of magnitude larger than subsequent gaps, and the remaining gaps are small and irregular; this profile is consistent with a dominant single-cluster resolution within each set and does not indicate a well-separated internal multi-cluster structure.

observations.meaning: Algorithmic eigengap screening resolution for each candidate set.
observations.finding: All four sets screen at the single-cluster resolution, so the partition-level screening does not provide feasible k>=2 internal solutions for any set.

observations.meaning: Average fused affinity across the current set boundaries for the relatively closest candidate pairs.
observations.finding: Between-set affinities are tightly clustered (approximately 0.00903 to 0.00908) and are only marginally below the within-set affinities, indicating that the current boundaries are not sharply separated in the fused geometry; the closest pair is K4_C0002–K4_C0004, but this is a pair-review entry point rather than a merge conclusion.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the cross-modal consistency dimension, the structural diagnostics describe how the four candidate sets are represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. The partition contains four sets of unequal size (39, 31, 20, 13 patients). Within-set affinity is uniformly high and similar across sets (about 0.0094–0.0101), while between-set affinities for the closest pairs are only slightly lower (about 0.00903–0.00908). This narrow within-versus-between margin indicates that the current set boundaries are not sharply delineated in the fused affinity geometry, even though each set is internally cohesive in absolute terms. The internal spectral profiles show a large leading eigengap in every set, but all four sets screen at candidate_k=1, meaning the dominant gap is located at the single-cluster resolution; the remaining eigengaps are small and irregular. Consequently, the partition-level screening does not identify feasible k>=2 internal subdivisions, and the large leading gaps should not be read as evidence of internal multi-cluster substructure. The nearest-pair affinities identify K4_C0002–K4_C0004 as the relatively closest boundary, followed by K4_C0001–K4_C0004 and K4_C0003–K4_C0004, but these are review entry points and do not by themselves indicate that any pair should be merged. Overall, the measurements indicate that the four sets are internally cohesive but weakly separated from one another in the fused geometry, with no partition-level evidence of internal subdivision.
reports.cross_evidence_context: No prior Evidence Reports are available for this request, so this report cannot be related to earlier interpreted evidence.
limitations: The structural diagnostics operate on the fused four-view affinity geometry and do not recluster patients or test alternative partitions.

Partition-level screening provides only the single-cluster resolution for each set and does not supply feasible k>=2 set-level solutions, so internal subdivision cannot be assessed from these results.
Between-set affinities are reported only for the relatively closest pairs; the full boundary structure across all set pairs is not enumerated.
The unequal set sizes (13–39 patients) mean that affinity summaries for the smallest set are based on fewer patients and may be less stable.
These measurements describe geometry within the supplied partition and do not establish biological coherence or independent validation.

observations.meaning: Computational estimability of the set-versus-rest GSEA for K4_C0002.
observations.finding: The enrichment analysis was estimable, with 19,449 finite Wald statistics entering the ranking.

observations.meaning: Sample counts for the K4_C0002-versus-rest contrast.
observations.finding: The contrast uses 31 target patients against a heterogeneous rest of 72 patients drawn from the other three candidate sets.

observations.meaning: Direction and strength of pathway enrichment relative to the K4_C0002-versus-rest Wald-statistic ranking, with GSEA FDR as pathway-level multiplicity correction.
observations.finding: K4_C0002 shows a strong, coherent up-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation (NES 2.788, FDR 0.001), protein secretion, fatty acid metabolism, adipogenesis, mTORC1 signaling, peroxisome, estrogen response, androgen response, bile acid metabolism, xenobiotic metabolism, ROS, cholesterol homeostasis, glycolysis, KRAS signaling up, and unfolded protein response (NES roughly 1.4-2.8, FDR < 0.05 for the top 16 pathways). Down-regulated pathways are weaker and mostly not significant after FDR correction (myogenesis, Wnt, angiogenesis, allograft rejection, Notch).

observations.meaning: Genes contributing most to the enrichment signal for representative up-regulated pathways.
observations.finding: The oxidative phosphorylation leading edge again comprises mitochondrial respiratory-chain and TCA-cycle genes, and the mTORC1 leading edge includes cholesterol synthesis, glycolysis, and proteostasis genes. This indicates coordinated up-regulation of mitochondrial energy metabolism and anabolic/growth programs in K4_C0002 relative to the rest.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the biological_support dimension, K4_C0002 exhibits a coherent and interpretable phenotype relative to the heterogeneous rest of the partition. The dominant signal is a strong up-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation (NES 2.788, FDR 0.001) with a leading edge of mitochondrial respiratory-chain and TCA-cycle genes, accompanied by up-regulation of protein secretion, fatty acid metabolism, adipogenesis, mTORC1 signaling, peroxisome, estrogen/androgen response, bile acid metabolism, xenobiotic metabolism, ROS, cholesterol homeostasis, glycolysis, KRAS signaling up, and unfolded protein response (NES roughly 1.4-2.8, FDR < 0.05 for the top 16 pathways). Down-regulated pathways are weaker and mostly not significant after FDR correction. The contrast uses 31 target patients against 72 rest patients, providing reasonable sample support, but the rest is a mixture of the other three candidate sets, so the enrichment is relative to a heterogeneous background. The multiplicity-adjusted FDR values support the coherence of the up-regulated program, but statistical significance alone does not establish biological importance, and the pathway-level results do not by themselves establish that K4_C0002 is a distinct biological subtype.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry, with no partition-level evidence of internal subdivision. The K4_C0002 enrichment profile is notable because it is the reciprocal of the K4_C0001 profile: K4_C0002 up-regulates oxidative phosphorylation and anabolic/growth programs, while K4_C0001 down-regulates oxidative phosphorylation and immune/inflammatory programs. This complementarity is consistent with the prior report's observation that K4_C0002 and K4_C0004 are the closest pair in the fused geometry, but the enrichment contrast is against the full heterogeneous rest, so it does not directly resolve the K4_C0002-K4_C0004 boundary. The strong oxidative phosphorylation signal in K4_C0002 also contrasts with the weak geometric separation, suggesting that the biological phenotype may be more distinct than the fused geometry alone indicates.
limitations: The rest group combines the other three candidate sets and is heterogeneous, so the set-versus-rest contrast is not a clean two-group biological comparison.
GSEA FDR values are pathway-level multiplicity corrections and do not establish biological importance or causality.
The ranking uses the unshrunken DESeq2 Wald statistic, not adjusted p-values or shrunken fold changes.
Pathway enrichment is derived from the RNA discovery view and does not provide independent validation.
The leading-edge gene lists are long and overlapping across pathways, so individual gene contributions should not be over-interpreted.

observations.meaning: Magnitude and statistical evidence of categorical technical/acquisition factor association with candidate membership, before and after multiple-testing correction.
observations.finding: Tissue source site shows the strongest categorical association (Cramer's V 0.342, q=0.003), followed by CT phase (0.263, q=0.0108), CT manufacturer (0.265, q=0.0108), CT scanner model (0.252, q=0.012), and CT reconstruction kernel (0.214, q=0.0257). All five categorical factors remain significant after BH correction.

observations.meaning: Effect magnitude and statistical evidence of continuous technical/acquisition factor association with candidate membership, before and after multiple-testing correction.
observations.finding: CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.195, q=0.00051) and CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.172, q=0.00075) show significant association with candidate membership. CT pixel spacing (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.473) and study year (epsilon-squared 0.009, q=0.305) do not.

observations.meaning: Observed factor-level imbalance contributing to the categorical associations.
observations.finding: Tissue source site is imbalanced: BP is overrepresented in K4_C0001 (24/39) and B8 is overrepresented in K4_C0002 (12/31). CT phase is imbalanced with UNKNOWN dominating K4_C0002 (15/31) and K4_C0003 (11/20), and MAIN_CE_HIGH concentrated in K4_C0001 (8/39).

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the confounder_exclusion dimension, the partition shows statistically significant association with multiple technical, acquisition, and site factors. Tissue source site has the strongest categorical association (Cramer's V 0.342, q=0.003), with BP overrepresented in K4_C0001 and B8 overrepresented in K4_C0002. CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT scanner model, and CT reconstruction kernel also show significant categorical associations (Cramer's V 0.214-0.265, q=0.0108-0.0257). Among continuous factors, CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.195, q=0.00051) and CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.172, q=0.00075) are significantly associated with candidate membership, while CT pixel spacing and study year are not. These associations indicate that the candidate partition is not independent of measured technical and acquisition factors, and the imbalance patterns suggest that some of the geometric or biological signal could be confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation, and the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition. The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH correction families, and the results should be interpreted within each family. The absence of significant association for CT pixel spacing and study year does not prove absence of confounding for those factors.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry. The confounder association results are relevant to that picture because the weak geometric separation could partly reflect technical or site-related structure rather than purely biological signal. In particular, the strong tissue source site association and the CT acquisition associations (z-spacing, slice thickness, phase, manufacturer, scanner model, kernel) suggest that the fused geometry may be influenced by technical factors. The biological_support reports for K4_C0001-K4_C0004 describe distinct biological phenotypes, but the confounder results indicate that these phenotypes could be partially confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics, which is an unresolved tension that matters for downstream review.
limitations: Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition.
Nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding.
The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH correction families, so p-values and q-values are not directly comparable across families.
The contingency tables show sparse cells for some factor levels, which can affect the stability of association estimates.
The analysis uses the supplied partition and does not test alternative partitions or adjust for multiple factors simultaneously.

observations.meaning: Association between candidate membership and clinical stratification variables.
observations.finding: Grade shows a nominally significant association (Cramer's V 0.215, p=0.015), with G4 enriched in K4_C0003 (9/20) and G2/G3 more evenly distributed. M stage, overall stage, and T stage do not show significant association.

observations.meaning: Set-versus-rest Fisher exact tests for M0/M1 imbalance within each candidate set.
observations.finding: K4_C0003 shows a nominally significant M1 enrichment (p=0.0352), with 6/20 M1 versus 8/83 in the rest. Other sets do not show significant M-stage imbalance.

observations.meaning: Agreement and chance-adjusted shared information between the candidate partition and established ccRCC taxonomies.
observations.finding: Correspondence with ClearCode34 (AMI 0.179, ARI 0.151) and TCGA m1-m4 (AMI 0.068, ARI 0.086) is low, indicating that the candidate partition does not closely reproduce these established taxonomies.

observations.meaning: Distribution of established taxonomy labels across candidate sets.
observations.finding: ClearCode34 ccA is concentrated in K4_C0001 (23/39) and ccB is concentrated in K4_C0002 (14/31) and K4_C0003 (13/20). TCGA m1 is concentrated in K4_C0001 (18/39), while m3 is concentrated in K4_C0003 (7/20).

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the known_label_echo dimension, the candidate partition shows limited correspondence with clinical stratification and established ccRCC taxonomies. Grade is the only clinical variable with a nominally significant association (Cramer's V 0.215, p=0.015), with G4 enriched in K4_C0003. M stage, overall stage, and T stage do not show significant association. The set-versus-rest Fisher tests show a nominally significant M1 enrichment in K4_C0003 (p=0.0352), but this is not corrected for multiple testing across sets and should be interpreted cautiously. Molecular taxonomy correspondence is low: ClearCode34 (AMI 0.179, ARI 0.151) and TCGA m1-m4 (AMI 0.068, ARI 0.086) both indicate weak agreement. The contingency tables show some concentration (e.g., ccA in K4_C0001, ccB in K4_C0002/K4_C0003, m1 in K4_C0001, m3 in K4_C0003), but the overall correspondence is weak. These results indicate that the candidate partition does not closely reproduce established clinical or molecular taxonomies, but this is taxonomy correspondence, not independent validation, and the RNA-derived taxonomies overlap the RNA discovery view.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry. The known_label_echo results are relevant because the weak correspondence with established taxonomies is consistent with the weak geometric separation, suggesting that the candidate partition may capture structure that is not aligned with standard clinical or molecular classifications. The biological_support reports describe distinct biological phenotypes for K4_C0001-K4_C0004, but the low taxonomy correspondence indicates that these phenotypes do not simply recapitulate ClearCode34 or TCGA m1-m4. The confounder_association report shows significant technical/site associations, which could contribute to the weak taxonomy correspondence if the partition is partly driven by technical factors.
limitations: TCGA m1-m4 and ClearCode34 overlap the RNA discovery view; this is taxonomy correspondence, not independent validation.
Clinical variables have varying coverage (m_stage missing_n=5), and some contingency cells are sparse.
The set-versus-rest Fisher tests are not corrected for multiple testing across sets.
The analysis uses the supplied partition and does not test alternative partitions.
Low correspondence does not establish that the partition is biologically invalid; it only indicates lack of alignment with these specific taxonomies.

observations.meaning: Computational estimability of the WXS mutation enrichment for K4_C0002.
observations.finding: The analysis was estimable, with 3,583 genes in the full nonsynonymous interpretation matrix tested and 31 target versus 72 rest patients.

observations.meaning: Sample counts for the K4_C0002-versus-rest mutation comparison.
observations.finding: The contrast uses 31 target patients against a heterogeneous rest of 72 patients drawn from the other three candidate sets.

observations.meaning: Driver-panel mutation enrichment or depletion in K4_C0002 versus the heterogeneous rest, with q_driver (within-panel BH) and q_global (full-matrix BH) as separate multiplicity questions.
observations.finding: VHL is strongly depleted in K4_C0002 (2/31 mutated versus 54/72 in the rest; OR 0.023, 95% CI 0.005-0.106; q_driver 9.7e-10, q_global 2.3e-07). PBRM1 is also depleted (5/31 versus 34/72; OR 0.215, 95% CI 0.074-0.622; q_driver 0.027, q_global 1.0). KDM5C (OR 5.19, q_driver 0.245) and TP53 (OR 17.8, q_driver 0.127) are enriched but do not survive driver-panel correction; CDKN2A has no events in either group.

observations.meaning: Limited display subset of non-driver genes with the largest nominal effects; every interpretation-matrix gene participates in q_global.
observations.finding: Several non-driver genes show large nominal target-enriched odds ratios (e.g., CPEB4 OR 23.7, p=0.0071; DNAH8 and GLB1 OR 17.8, p=0.025), but none reaches q_global significance (all q_global 1.0), consistent with sparse mutation counts and wide intervals.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the biological_support dimension, the WXS mutation profile of K4_C0002 is coherent and interpretable relative to the heterogeneous rest of the partition, but its dominant feature is depletion rather than enrichment of canonical ccRCC drivers. VHL mutation is markedly less frequent in K4_C0002 (2/31, 6.5%) than in the rest (54/72, 75%), with an odds ratio of 0.023 (95% CI 0.005-0.106) that survives both within-driver-panel correction (q_driver 9.7e-10) and full-matrix correction (q_global 2.3e-07). PBRM1 is similarly depleted (5/31 versus 34/72; OR 0.215, 95% CI 0.074-0.622; q_driver 0.027) but does not survive the full-matrix correction (q_global 1.0). On the enriched side, KDM5C (OR 5.19) and TP53 (OR 17.8) have nominal Fisher evidence (p=0.065 and p=0.025) but do not survive driver-panel correction (q_driver 0.245 and 0.127), and their intervals are wide and include one. CDKN2A has no events in either group, so its effect is not estimable. The exploratory non-driver genes with the largest nominal effects (CPEB4, DNAH8, GLB1) all have q_global 1.0, indicating that no individual gene outside the driver panel reaches full-matrix significance. Taken together, the mutation data indicate that K4_C0002 is characterized by a relative absence of VHL and PBRM1 mutations compared with the rest of the partition, which is a coherent and biologically interpretable contrast in ccRCC, but the driver panel is a post-hoc annotation rather than a discovery feature set, the rest group is a heterogeneous mixture of the other three sets, and the sparse mutation counts limit precision. Statistical significance alone does not establish biological importance, and these results do not by themselves establish that K4_C0002 is a distinct biological subtype.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior RNA pathway enrichment report for K4_C0002 described strong up-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation and anabolic/growth programs (OXPHOS NES 2.788, FDR 0.001; mTORC1, fatty acid metabolism, adipogenesis, protein secretion all FDR 0.001) relative to the heterogeneous rest. The WXS result is complementary in direction: K4_C0002 is depleted for VHL and PBRM1 mutations, the canonical ccRCC tumor-suppressor drivers, while showing nominal enrichment of KDM5C and TP53. This is a biologically coherent pairing in the sense that a VHL/PBRM1-low, OXPHOS-high phenotype is a recognizable axis in ccRCC, but the two modalities are not independent confirmations of the same boundary: the RNA contrast is against the full heterogeneous rest, and the WXS contrast is likewise set-versus-rest, so neither resolves the K4_C0002-K4_C0004 boundary that the structural_diagnostics report flagged as the closest pair. The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry; the WXS depletion signal is stronger than that weak geometric separation would suggest, which is an unresolved tension. The prior confounder_association report showed significant tissue source site and CT acquisition associations with candidate membership, so some of the mutation contrast could in principle be confounded by site or acquisition characteristics, though mutation status is less directly tied to imaging acquisition than expression is.
limitations: The rest group combines the other three candidate sets and is heterogeneous, so the set-versus-rest contrast is not a clean two-group biological comparison.
The driver panel is a post-hoc prespecified ccRCC annotation, not a discovery feature-selection criterion; q_driver and q_global answer different multiplicity questions and should not be conflated.
Mutation counts are sparse (e.g., VHL 2/31 in the target, PBRM1 5/31), so odds ratios and intervals are imprecise and several genes have zero cells requiring Haldane-Anscombe correction.
CDKN2A is not estimable because neither group has mutation events.
Exploratory non-driver genes are a limited display subset; none reaches q_global significance, and individual gene effects should not be over-interpreted.
WXS mutation enrichment is derived from the mutation interpretation matrix and does not provide independent validation of the partition.

observations.meaning: PERMANOVA location association and PERMDISP dispersion test for tissue source site in the fused patient-distance geometry.
observations.finding: Tissue source site shows a significant PERMANOVA location association with the fused geometry (pseudo-F 1.014, p=0.001, q=0.0025, r_squared 0.050), while PERMDISP is not significant (p=0.434), so the location association is not accompanied by detectable dispersion differences across sites.

observations.meaning: PERMANOVA location association and PERMDISP dispersion test for CT phase in the CT native-distance geometry.
observations.finding: CT phase shows the largest categorical CT association (pseudo-F 2.466, p=0.001, q=0.0025, r_squared 0.154) and also a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (p=0.019, q=0.0285), so the location association may reflect both centroid and dispersion differences.

observations.meaning: PERMANOVA location association and PERMDISP dispersion test for CT manufacturer in the CT native-distance geometry.
observations.finding: CT manufacturer shows a significant PERMANOVA association (pseudo-F 3.118, p=0.004, q=0.0067, r_squared 0.059) and a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (p=0.003, q=0.009), with the Philips level having only 3 patients.

permdisp.reason: PERMDISP requires at least two observations in every group.

permdisp.reason: PERMDISP requires at least two observations in every group.

observations.meaning: PERMANOVA location association and PERMDISP dispersion test for CT scanner model in the CT native-distance geometry.
observations.finding: CT scanner model shows a nominal PERMANOVA association (pseudo-F 1.453, p=0.054, q=0.054, r_squared 0.200) that does not reach BH-corrected significance; PERMDISP is not estimable because many of the 16 scanner-model levels have fewer than two observations.

observations.meaning: Distance-based regression of continuous acquisition factors on CT native-distance geometry, with its own BH family.
observations.finding: CT z-spacing (pseudo-F 16.67, q=0.002, r_squared 0.142) and CT slice thickness (pseudo-F 15.85, q=0.002, r_squared 0.136) show the strongest continuous associations; CT pixel spacing (q=0.035, r_squared 0.019) and study year (q=0.004, r_squared 0.029) are also significant but with much smaller magnitudes.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the confounder_exclusion dimension, the partition shows statistically significant association with multiple technical, acquisition, and site factors, and the pattern is broad rather than isolated. In the fused geometry, tissue source site has a significant PERMANOVA location association (pseudo-F 1.014, p=0.001, q=0.0025) with a small r_squared of 0.050, and PERMDISP is not significant (p=0.434), so the site association is not accompanied by detectable dispersion differences. In the CT native-distance geometry, CT phase has the largest categorical association (pseudo-F 2.466, q=0.0025, r_squared 0.154) and also a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (q=0.0285), so its location association may reflect both centroid and dispersion differences. CT manufacturer is significant in both PERMANOVA (q=0.0067, r_squared 0.059) and PERMDISP (q=0.009), but the Philips level has only 3 patients, so that dispersion result is based on very few observations. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and CT scanner model (q=0.054) are nominally associated but do not survive BH correction, and their PERMDISP tests are not estimable because several levels have fewer than two observations. Among continuous acquisition factors, CT z-spacing (pseudo-F 16.67, q=0.002, r_squared 0.142) and CT slice thickness (pseudo-F 15.85, q=0.002, r_squared 0.136) show the strongest associations, with CT pixel spacing (q=0.035, r_squared 0.019) and study year (q=0.004, r_squared 0.029) significant but much smaller in magnitude. The categorical PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression tests belong to separate BH families, so their q-values are not directly comparable across families. These results indicate that the candidate partition is not independent of measured technical and acquisition factors, and the combination of a significant site association in the fused geometry with strong CT acquisition associations in the CT geometry suggests that some of the geometric or biological signal could be confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation, the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition, and the nonsignificant PERMDISP for tissue source site does not prove absence of confounding.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry, with no partition-level evidence of internal subdivision. The confounder results are relevant to that picture because the weak geometric separation could partly reflect technical or site-related structure rather than purely biological signal: the significant tissue source site association in the fused geometry and the strong CT z-spacing and slice thickness associations in the CT geometry indicate that the fused and CT geometries are not independent of measured technical factors. The prior biological_support reports for K4_C0001-K4_C0004 describe distinct RNA phenotypes (K4_C0001 broad OXPHOS/immune down-regulation, K4_C0002 OXPHOS/anabolic up-regulation, K4_C0003 immune/inflammatory up-regulation, K4_C0004 OXPHOS down-regulation with EMT/Hedgehog up-regulation), and the WXS report for K4_C0002 shows VHL/PBRM1 depletion. The confounder results create an unresolved tension with those biological interpretations: if site and CT acquisition factors are associated with candidate membership, some of the apparent biological distinctiveness could be partially confounded, and the biological reports do not adjust for these factors. The prior known_label_echo report showed low correspondence with ClearCode34 and TCGA m1-m4, which is also consistent with the partition capturing structure that is not aligned with standard taxonomies and could be partly technical.
limitations: Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition.
Nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding; the nonsignificant PERMDISP for tissue source site does not prove no dispersion confounding.
The categorical PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression tests belong to separate BH families, so p-values and q-values are not directly comparable across families.

observations.meaning: Effect magnitude and statistical evidence of continuous technical/acquisition factor association with K4_C0002 membership, before and after BH correction within the continuous family.
observations.finding: CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.174, q=7.43e-05) and CT z-spacing (0.180, q=7.43e-05) are strongly and significantly associated with K4_C0002 membership; study year and pixel spacing are not significant.

observations.meaning: Observed factor-level imbalance contributing to the categorical associations for K4_C0002.
observations.finding: B8 is overrepresented in K4_C0002 (12/31 versus 7/72 in the rest) and BP underrepresented (7/31 versus 38/72); Siemens is overrepresented (17/31 versus 13/72) and GE underrepresented (14/31 versus 56/72); B30f kernel is overrepresented (9/31 versus 4/72). These imbalances drive the corrected associations.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the confounder_exclusion dimension, K4_C0002 shows strong and BH-corrected associations with multiple technical, acquisition, and site factors. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.428, q=0.0018), CT manufacturer (0.353, q=0.0018), CT reconstruction kernel (0.387, q=0.0018), and CT scanner model (0.374, q=0.0075) are all significantly associated with K4_C0002 membership, and CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.174, q=7.43e-05) and CT z-spacing (0.180, q=7.43e-05) show the strongest continuous associations. The imbalance patterns are substantial: B8 overrepresentation, Siemens overrepresentation, and B30f kernel overrepresentation. These results indicate that K4_C0002 membership is not independent of measured site and CT acquisition characteristics, and the magnitude of the associations (Cramer's V up to 0.43, epsilon-squared up to 0.18) is larger than for K4_C0001. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation, and the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition. The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH families, so q-values are not directly comparable across families. The strong confounder signal for K4_C0002 is an unresolved concern for interpreting its biological phenotype.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior biological_support reports for K4_C0002 described strong OXPHOS/anabolic up-regulation (NES 2.788, FDR 0.001) and the WXS report showed VHL/PBRM1 depletion. The present confounder results show that K4_C0002 has the strongest corrected technical and site associations in the partition, which creates a material tension: the biological and mutation phenotypes could be partially confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics, and the biological reports do not adjust for these factors. The prior structural_diagnostics report noted weak geometric separation, and the strong confounder signal for K4_C0002 is consistent with the possibility that some of its geometric or biological distinctiveness reflects technical structure. The prior partition-level confounder_association report found corrected tissue source site and CT acquisition associations across the partition; the K4_C0002 set-level results are consistent with and contribute to that partition-level pattern.
limitations: Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the tests do not establish that these factors drive K4_C0002 membership.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For the K4_C0001-K4_C0002 pair, the four-view geometry shows a consistent but weak boundary. In each modality the mean between-label distance exceeds the mean within-label distance, but the native-distance silhouettes are small in CT (0.043), RNA (0.056), and WSI (0.051), and only moderately larger in WXS (0.184). This means the current two-set labels are only faintly expressed in three of the four native geometries, with the mutation view providing the clearest (though still modest) separation. The global geometry concordance between modalities is modest (GRV 0.14-0.20) and all permutation tests reject exchangeable patient correspondence, but GRV describes overall shared patient geometry rather than support for this specific boundary; the modest values indicate the views are not redundant and may carry complementary structure. The bootstrap intervals for GRV are moderately wide, so the magnitude of shared geometry is not tightly pinned. Taken together, the measurements indicate that K4_C0001 and K4_C0002 are distinguishable but not sharply separated in any single native geometry, and the weak pair separation does not by itself indicate that the pair should be merged.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry, with K4_C0001-K4_C0002 among the closer pairs. The present pair-level native-distance results are consistent with that picture: the boundary is weakly expressed in CT, RNA, and WSI, with WXS somewhat stronger. The prior biological_support reports described K4_C0001 as OXPHOS/immune down-regulated and K4_C0002 as OXPHOS/anabolic up-regulated, and the WXS report showed VHL/PBRM1 depletion in K4_C0002; these biological contrasts are more pronounced than the weak native-distance separation, an unresolved tension. The prior confounder reports showed corrected site and CT acquisition associations for K4_C0002, which could contribute to the modest geometry differences observed here.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Within the cross_modal_consistency dimension, the fused four-view geometry represents K4_C0001 and K4_C0002 as internally cohesive but barely separated. Both sets have high within-set affinity (about 0.00944), and the between-set affinity (about 0.00904) is only slightly lower, yielding a boundary silhouette of essentially zero (0.00041). The union spectral profile shows a large leading eigengap (0.383) at candidate_k=1, with the remaining gaps three orders of magnitude smaller; this indicates that the dominant spectral resolution of the union is the single-cluster resolution, so the union eigengap does not identify a feasible internal subdivision and should not be read as evidence of multi-cluster substructure. The measurements therefore indicate that the current K4_C0001/K4_C0002 boundary is not sharply delineated in the fused geometry, even though each set is internally cohesive in absolute terms. This weak pair separation is a description of the supplied labels and does not by itself indicate that the pair should be merged.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: Within the cross-modal consistency dimension, the structural diagnostics describe how the four candidate sets are represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. The partition contains four sets of unequal size (39, 31, 20, 13 patients). Within-set affinity is uniformly high and similar across sets (about 0.0094–0.0101), while between-set affinities for the closest pairs are only slightly lower (about 0.00903–0.00908). This narrow within-versus-between margin indicates that the current set boundaries are not sharply delineated in the fused affinity geometry, even though each set is internally cohesive in absolute terms. The internal spectral profiles show a large leading eigengap in every set, but all four sets screen at candidate_k=1, meaning the dominant gap is located at the single-cluster resolution; the remaining eigengaps are small and irregular. Consequently, the partition-level screening does not identify feasible k>=2 internal subdivisions, and the large leading gaps should not be read as evidence of internal multi-cluster substructure. The nearest-pair affinities identify K4_C0002–K4_C0004 as the relatively closest boundary, followed by K4_C0001–K4_C0004 and K4_C0003–K4_C0004, but these are review entry points and do not by themselves indicate that any pair should be merged. Overall, the measurements indicate that the four sets are internally cohesive but weakly separated from one another in the fused geometry, with no partition-level evidence of internal subdivision.

observations.meaning: Computational estimability of the set-versus-rest GSEA for K4_C0003.
observations.finding: The enrichment analysis was estimable, with 19,449 finite Wald statistics entering the ranking.

observations.meaning: Sample counts for the K4_C0003-versus-rest contrast.

observations.meaning: Direction and strength of pathway enrichment relative to the K4_C0003-versus-rest Wald-statistic ranking, with GSEA FDR as pathway-level multiplicity correction.
observations.finding: K4_C0003 shows a strong, coherent up-regulation of immune/inflammatory pathways: allograft rejection (NES 2.816, FDR 0.001), interferon gamma (NES 2.410, FDR 0.001), interferon alpha (NES 2.336, FDR 0.001), IL6-JAK-STAT3 (NES 2.327, FDR 0.001), inflammatory response (NES 1.977, FDR 0.001), and complement (NES 1.848, FDR 0.001). Down-regulated pathways include UV-response-DN, protein secretion, androgen response, fatty acid metabolism, bile acid metabolism, and heme metabolism (NES roughly -1.6 to -2.1, FDR < 0.05 for the top seven).

observations.meaning: Genes contributing most to the enrichment signal for representative up-regulated pathways.
observations.finding: The allograft rejection and interferon gamma leading edges are dominated by HLA class I/II genes, interferon-stimulated genes, T-cell and antigen-presentation genes, and chemokines. This indicates coordinated up-regulation of immune/inflammatory and antigen-presentation programs in K4_C0003 relative to the rest.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: Within the biological_support dimension, K4_C0003 exhibits a coherent and interpretable phenotype relative to the heterogeneous rest of the partition. The dominant signal is a strong up-regulation of immune/inflammatory pathways: allograft rejection (NES 2.816, FDR 0.001), interferon gamma (NES 2.410, FDR 0.001), interferon alpha (NES 2.336, FDR 0.001), IL6-JAK-STAT3 (NES 2.327, FDR 0.001), inflammatory response (NES 1.977, FDR 0.001), and complement (NES 1.848, FDR 0.001). The leading edges are dominated by HLA class I/II genes, interferon-stimulated genes, T-cell and antigen-presentation genes, and chemokines, indicating a coordinated immune/inflammatory program. Down-regulated pathways include UV-response-DN, protein secretion, androgen response, fatty acid metabolism, bile acid metabolism, and heme metabolism (NES roughly -1.6 to -2.1, FDR < 0.05 for the top seven). The contrast uses 20 target patients against 83 rest patients, providing reasonable sample support, but the rest is a mixture of the other three candidate sets, so the enrichment is relative to a heterogeneous background. The multiplicity-adjusted FDR values support the coherence of the up-regulated immune program, but statistical significance alone does not establish biological importance, and the pathway-level results do not by themselves establish that K4_C0003 is a distinct biological subtype.
biological_support.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry, with no partition-level evidence of internal subdivision. The K4_C0003 enrichment profile is notable because it is the reciprocal of the K4_C0001 profile: K4_C0003 up-regulates immune/inflammatory and interferon programs, while K4_C0001 down-regulates those same programs. This complementarity is consistent with the prior report's observation that K4_C0003 is one of the smaller sets (20 patients) and that K4_C0003-K4_C0004 is among the closer pairs in the fused geometry, but the enrichment contrast is against the full heterogeneous rest, so it does not directly resolve the K4_C0003-K4_C0004 boundary. The strong immune/inflammatory signal in K4_C0003 also contrasts with the weak geometric separation, suggesting that the biological phenotype may be more distinct than the fused geometry alone indicates.
limitations: The rest group combines the other three candidate sets and is heterogeneous, so the set-versus-rest contrast is not a clean two-group biological comparison.
GSEA FDR values are pathway-level multiplicity corrections and do not establish biological importance or causality.
The ranking uses the unshrunken DESeq2 Wald statistic, not adjusted p-values or shrunken fold changes.
Pathway enrichment is derived from the RNA discovery view and does not provide independent validation.
The leading-edge gene lists are long and overlapping across pathways, so individual gene contributions should not be over-interpreted.

known_label_echo.dimension_interpretation: Within the known_label_echo dimension, the candidate partition shows limited correspondence with clinical stratification and established ccRCC taxonomies. Grade is the only clinical variable with a nominally significant association (Cramer's V 0.215, p=0.015), with G4 enriched in K4_C0003. M stage, overall stage, and T stage do not show significant association. The set-versus-rest Fisher tests show a nominally significant M1 enrichment in K4_C0003 (p=0.0352), but this is not corrected for multiple testing across sets and should be interpreted cautiously. Molecular taxonomy correspondence is low: ClearCode34 (AMI 0.179, ARI 0.151) and TCGA m1-m4 (AMI 0.068, ARI 0.086) both indicate weak agreement. The contingency tables show some concentration (e.g., ccA in K4_C0001, ccB in K4_C0002/K4_C0003, m1 in K4_C0001, m3 in K4_C0003), but the overall correspondence is weak. These results indicate that the candidate partition does not closely reproduce established clinical or molecular taxonomies, but this is taxonomy correspondence, not independent validation, and the RNA-derived taxonomies overlap the RNA discovery view.
known_label_echo.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry. The known_label_echo results are relevant because the weak correspondence with established taxonomies is consistent with the weak geometric separation, suggesting that the candidate partition may capture structure that is not aligned with standard clinical or molecular classifications. The biological_support reports describe distinct biological phenotypes for K4_C0001-K4_C0004, but the low taxonomy correspondence indicates that these phenotypes do not simply recapitulate ClearCode34 or TCGA m1-m4. The confounder_association report shows significant technical/site associations, which could contribute to the weak taxonomy correspondence if the partition is partly driven by technical factors.

All five categorical factors remain significant after BH correction.

observations.finding: CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.195, q=0.00051) and CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.172, q=0.00075) show significant association with candidate membership. CT pixel spacing (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.473) and study year (epsilon-squared 0.009, q=0.305) do not.

observations.finding: Tissue source site is imbalanced: BP is overrepresented in K4_C0001 (24/39) and B8 is overrepresented in K4_C0002 (12/31). CT phase is imbalanced with UNKNOWN dominating K4_C0002 (15/31) and K4_C0003 (11/20), and MAIN_CE_HIGH concentrated in K4_C0001 (8/39).

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: Within the confounder_exclusion dimension, the partition shows statistically significant association with multiple technical, acquisition, and site factors. Tissue source site has the strongest categorical association (Cramer's V 0.342, q=0.003), with BP overrepresented in K4_C0001 and B8 overrepresented in K4_C0002. CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT scanner model, and CT reconstruction kernel also show significant categorical associations (Cramer's V 0.214-0.265, q=0.0108-0.0257). Among continuous factors, CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.195, q=0.00051) and CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.172, q=0.00075) are significantly associated with candidate membership, while CT pixel spacing and study year are not. These associations indicate that the candidate partition is not independent of measured technical and acquisition factors, and the imbalance patterns suggest that some of the geometric or biological signal could be confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation, and the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition. The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH correction families, and the results should be interpreted within each family. The absence of significant association for CT pixel spacing and study year does not prove absence of confounding for those factors.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry. The confounder association results are relevant to that picture because the weak geometric separation could partly reflect technical or site-related structure rather than purely biological signal. In particular, the strong tissue source site association and the CT acquisition associations (z-spacing, slice thickness, phase, manufacturer, scanner model, kernel) suggest that the fused geometry may be influenced by technical factors. The biological_support reports for K4_C0001-K4_C0004 describe distinct biological phenotypes, but the confounder results indicate that these phenotypes could be partially confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics, which is an unresolved tension that matters for downstream review.
limitations: Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition.
Nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding.
The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH correction families, so p-values and q-values are not directly comparable across families.

The analysis uses the supplied partition and does not test alternative partitions or adjust for multiple factors simultaneously.

observations.finding: CT manufacturer shows a significant PERMANOVA association (pseudo-F 3.118, p=0.004, q=0.0067, r_squared 0.059) and a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (p=0.003, q=0.009), with the Philips level having only 3 patients.

permdisp.reason: PERMDISP requires at least two observations in every group.

observations.finding: CT scanner model shows a nominal PERMANOVA association (pseudo-F 1.453, p=0.054, q=0.054, r_squared 0.200) that does not reach BH-corrected significance; PERMDISP is not estimable because many of the 16 scanner-model levels have fewer than two observations.

observations.meaning: Distance-based regression of continuous acquisition factors on CT native-distance geometry, with its own BH family.
observations.finding: CT z-spacing (pseudo-F 16.67, q=0.002, r_squared 0.142) and CT slice thickness (pseudo-F 15.85, q=0.002, r_squared 0.136) show the strongest continuous associations; CT pixel spacing (q=0.035, r_squared 0.019) and study year (q=0.004, r_squared 0.029) are also significant but with much smaller magnitudes.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: Within the confounder_exclusion dimension, the partition shows statistically significant association with multiple technical, acquisition, and site factors, and the pattern is broad rather than isolated. In the fused geometry, tissue source site has a significant PERMANOVA location association (pseudo-F 1.014, p=0.001, q=0.0025) with a small r_squared of 0.050, and PERMDISP is not significant (p=0.434), so the site association is not accompanied by detectable dispersion differences. In the CT native-distance geometry, CT phase has the largest categorical association (pseudo-F 2.466, q=0.0025, r_squared 0.154) and also a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (q=0.0285), so its location association may reflect both centroid and dispersion differences. CT manufacturer is significant in both PERMANOVA (q=0.0067, r_squared 0.059) and PERMDISP (q=0.009), but the Philips level has only 3 patients, so that dispersion result is based on very few observations. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and CT scanner model (q=0.054) are nominally associated but do not survive BH correction, and their PERMDISP tests are not estimable because several levels have fewer than two observations. Among continuous acquisition factors, CT z-spacing (pseudo-F 16.67, q=0.002, r_squared 0.142) and CT slice thickness (pseudo-F 15.85, q=0.002, r_squared 0.136) show the strongest associations, with CT pixel spacing (q=0.035, r_squared 0.019) and study year (q=0.004, r_squared 0.029) significant but much smaller in magnitude. The categorical PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression tests belong to separate BH families, so their q-values are not directly comparable across families. These results indicate that the candidate partition is not independent of measured technical and acquisition factors, and the combination of a significant site association in the fused geometry with strong CT acquisition associations in the CT geometry suggests that some of the geometric or biological signal could be confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics. However, association is not proof of technical artifact or causation, the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition, and the nonsignificant PERMDISP for tissue source site does not prove absence of confounding.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural_diagnostics report described the four sets as internally cohesive but weakly separated in the fused geometry, with no partition-level evidence of internal subdivision. The confounder results are relevant to that picture because the weak geometric separation could partly reflect technical or site-related structure rather than purely biological signal: the significant tissue source site association in the fused geometry and the strong CT z-spacing and slice thickness associations in the CT geometry indicate that the fused and CT geometries are not independent of measured technical factors. The prior biological_support reports for K4_C0001-K4_C0004 describe distinct RNA phenotypes (K4_C0001 broad OXPHOS/immune down-regulation, K4_C0002 OXPHOS/anabolic up-regulation, K4_C0003 immune/inflammatory up-regulation, K4_C0004 OXPHOS down-regulation with EMT/Hedgehog up-regulation), and the WXS report for K4_C0002 shows VHL/PBRM1 depletion. The confounder results create an unresolved tension with those biological interpretations: if site and CT acquisition factors are associated with candidate membership, some of the apparent biological distinctiveness could be partially confounded, and the biological reports do not adjust for these factors. The prior known_label_echo report showed low correspondence with ClearCode34 and TCGA m1-m4, which is also consistent with the partition capturing structure that is not aligned with standard taxonomies and could be partly technical.
limitations: Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition.
Nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding; the nonsignificant PERMDISP for tissue source site does not prove no dispersion confounding.
The categorical PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression tests belong to separate BH families, so p-values and q-values are not directly comparable across families.

Several factor levels are sparse (e.g., CT manufacturer Philips n=3; many scanner-model and kernel levels with fewer than two observations), which makes PERMDISP not estimable for kernel and scanner model and can destabilize association estimates.

observations.meaning: Observed factor-level imbalance contributing to the categorical associations for K4_C0003.
observations.finding: CJ is strongly overrepresented in K4_C0003 (8/20 versus 3/83 in the rest) and BP underrepresented (6/20 versus 39/83); UNKNOWN CT phase is overrepresented (11/20 versus 29/83). These imbalances drive the corrected site association and the nominal phase association.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: Within the confounder_exclusion dimension, K4_C0003 shows a significant BH-corrected association with tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.443, q=0.009), driven by strong CJ overrepresentation (8/20 versus 3/83 in the rest). CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.0819, q=0.0105) and CT slice thickness (0.0535, q=0.0342) are also significantly associated with K4_C0003 membership, though with smaller magnitudes than for K4_C0002. CT phase is nominally associated (0.292, p=0.026) but does not survive correction (q=0.0585), and CT manufacturer, scanner model, and reconstruction kernel are not significantly associated. The sample is 20 target versus 83 rest patients, so the tests have moderate power, and the small set size makes the estimates more sensitive to individual patients. Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation, and the tests do not establish that these factors drive the partition. The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH families, so q-values are not directly comparable across families. The corrected site association and the significant CT acquisition associations are unresolved concerns for interpreting the K4_C0003 biological phenotype.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: The prior biological_support report for K4_C0003 described strong immune/inflammatory up-regulation (allograft rejection NES 2.816, FDR 0.001; interferon gamma NES 2.410, FDR 0.001). The present confounder results show a corrected tissue source site association and significant CT z-spacing and slice thickness associations for K4_C0003, which creates a material tension: the immune phenotype could be partially confounded by site and CT acquisition characteristics, and the biological report does not adjust for these factors. The prior structural_diagnostics report noted weak geometric separation, and the corrected site association for K4_C0003 is consistent with the possibility that some of its geometric or biological distinctiveness reflects site structure. The prior partition-level confounder_association report found corrected tissue source site and CT acquisition associations across the partition; the K4_C0003 set-level results are consistent with and contribute to that partition-level pattern.
limitations: Association is not proof of technical artifact or causation; the tests do not establish that these factors drive K4_C0003 membership.
Nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding; CT phase is nominally associated but not corrected.
The categorical and continuous factors belong to separate BH correction families, so p-values and q-values are not directly comparable across families.
The target set is small (20 patients), so association estimates are less stable and more sensitive to individual patients.
